records.updated_content: Bare-metal: single loop, no OS scheduler; suitable when the workload is stable, latency-sensitive, and tightly bounded, because the developer owns task ordering and there is no scheduler-induced jitter. RTOS: preemptive multitasking with scheduling guarantees; better when systems must multiplex tasks with bounded worst-case latency, priority inheritance, and deadline-aware dispatch, but scheduler behavior introduces determinism trade-offs the original answer did not explain.

records.original_issue: The original finance concept is correct, but it is too thin for training usefulness because it lacks the operational reasoning behind the formula: how expected return, expected inflation, risk premium, and planning horizon change the practical interpretation of present value and discount rate choice.
records.repair_applied: Added 3 disciplined expansions: (1) investment return rationale, (2) rate/inflation sensitivity, (3) horizon dependency, while preserving the original PV formula.
records.proposed_fix: Expand time-value-of-money rationale to include investment return, rate/inflation sensitivity, and horizon dependency alongside the existing formula.
records.updated_content: Money today is worth more than the same nominal amount in the future because it can be invested to earn a return; retaining liquidity also avoids forced future consumption at unfavorable prices. Present value therefore depends not only on the formula PV = FV/(1+r)^n, but also on the expected real return after inflation, the chosen discount rate, and the planning horizon over which cash flows are compared.
